analysis.title: "Last Chopper Out Of Saigon": The Skeptics Line Up As Anthropic's $1.5 Trillion Debut Meets A 99-Cent DeepSeek
key_insights: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83, $5 above the top of the range, and upsized to 980 million shares, raising more than $107 billion including a $26 billion vendor placement (Google, Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft, TSMC). That is roughly $1.1 trillion on shares outstanding or about $1.5 trillion fully diluted.
Per Bloomberg, ANT was indicated up to 24% higher on the gray market before the first trade, with Nasdaq 100 futures up 2%. Hedge funds are 11 points underweight tech, so some may have to chase.

Seaport's Jay Goldberg argues open-weight models are a weaker threat to Anthropic than its prospectus suggests. Self-hosting a model on reserved AWS instances only makes sense for customers spending more than $2.4 million a year, because reserved GPUs sit idle outside peak hours.

On Seaport's chart, DeepSeek V4 Pro falls below Claude Opus 5.5 pricing only at about the $2.4 million-a-year spend level. Kimi K3 stays above Opus even at a trillion-plus tokens a month. Claude Haiku 5.5 at $0.20 per million tokens is the cheapest line, versus $0.99 for DeepSeek V4 Pro from its cheapest host.

Per the S-1/A, Anthropic has 11,900 customers spending over $100,000 a year, about 1,900 over $1 million and 250 over $10 million. The article notes the customers who can rationally self-host are the largest spenders, and the S-1 does not break out revenue by tier. On Seaport's chart DeepSeek V4 Pro falls to about $0.50 per million tokens at high volume, about a sixteenth of Opus.

Third-party hosts such as AWS Bedrock are cheaper for many customers but offer less security and fewer features than going direct. Anthropic sells nearly half its revenue through hyperscaler cloud marketplaces, which also rent DeepSeek, Kimi and GLM.

Anthropic has defended against open weights mostly by cutting prices. Token prices fell 50% in one month. Price cuts and discounts removed about $600 million from Q3 revenue, compute rose to 58% of sales from 48%, and revenue per compute dollar fell to $1.72 from $2.08. The first operating profit lasted one quarter.

The article lists two factors outside Seaport's model: GPU rental prices for all but the newest chips have been falling since September, which lowers the $2.4 million breakeven, and Anthropic's frontier lead can be copied (the White House alleged in July that Moonshot distilled Anthropic's Fable, and Anthropic launched its newest Fable at a 20% discount).

The article argues a federal crackdown on open-weight models has become more likely after Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia, and David Sacks says Anthropic's allies have wanted one. Anthropic says it has never advocated a ban.

On Seaport's 16.25 billion diluted shares, $83 is about $1.35 trillion, or about 8.8x 2027 revenue of $153.9 billion and about 39x 2028 EPS of $2.13 (article's arithmetic). Goldberg carries no rating or price target and sees a 2027 adjusted loss of $0.96 per share. At $103 the multiple is about 48x 2028 EPS.
Seaport's path implies revenue from $4.6 billion in 2025 to $317 billion in 2028, about 69x in three years, with $109.5 billion of debt and a compute bill of roughly $900 billion.

Bloomberg Intelligence (Mandeep Singh, William Tong) puts the deal at about $1.5 trillion, 12-13x expected 2027 sales. Bloomberg's one-year forward price-to-sales is 11.1x. The article calculates the market is underwriting $115-135 billion of 2027 revenue, $20-40 billion below Seaport's figure, so ANT trades at 9x to 13x next year's sales.
Per Bloomberg Opinion, only Tesla and Eli Lilly among trillion-dollar companies trade at a higher price-to-sales multiple (SpaceX tied at 11.1x). Alphabet, Nvidia, Meta and Amazon trade at 3x to 6x.

Bloomberg Intelligence says the pricing assumes recursive self-improvement lowering compute costs and opening areas such as drug discovery, first-party agents sustaining net revenue retention against Google's Gemini and Meta's Muse, and execution on enterprise adoption and API monetization, while token-price pressure intensifies.
Amundi CIO Vincent Mortier calls the valuation 'a bit excessive', citing unproven returns on AI investment across players.

Bloomberg Opinion's Nir Kaissar says buyers using ANT as an AI-disruption hedge already own it. Amazon and Alphabet are about 9% of the S&P 500 and will hold 28% of Anthropic, giving index holders a look-through stake of about 3%. He notes IPOs often slump afterward and SpaceX is down about 30% from its post-IPO high.

Kaissar argues the payoff is limited by size: Nvidia was worth 0.04% of Anthropic's expected IPO valuation when it listed. The article calculates repeating Nvidia's run implies a 2,500x gain, about $3.75 quadrillion.

Kaissar sees shallow moats for large language models, with easy replication and limited brand loyalty. He flags that Amazon and Alphabet are both partners and competitors, and that windfall profits and midterm-driven data center restrictions could invite regulation that would help incumbents trading at half the multiple.

Morgan Stanley's Matthew Hornbach says damage from a breach of AI safeguards is the biggest risk currently underpriced by markets. Seaport's risk section lists a system escaping constraints or being used in a cyberattack on Anthropic.
The article's view is that Anthropic can keep its lead by cutting prices or keep its margins, not both, and the next couple of quarterly reports will show which gave.

market_movers.rationale: Anthropic IPO priced at $83 and indicated up to 24% higher on the gray market. Seaport carries no rating or price target.

sector_views.rationale: Hedge funds are 11 points underweight tech, which may force chasing into the Anthropic debut. Megacaps trade at 3x to 6x forward sales versus 9x to 13x for ANT.

earnings_insights: Seaport (Goldberg) 2027 estimates for Anthropic: revenue $153.9 billion and adjusted loss of $0.96 per share. 2028 EPS estimate $2.13. These are Seaport forecasts, not reported figures.

S-1/A Q3 figures, as reported: price cuts and discounts reduced revenue by about $600 million, compute and infrastructure were 58% of sales versus 48% previously, revenue per dollar of compute was $1.72 versus $2.08, and the first operating profit lasted one quarter.
Seaport's revenue path is $4.6 billion in 2025 to $317 billion in 2028 (forecast).
crypto_views: The pre-IPO overhang had investors selling gold, crypto and Nvidia to make room for the allocation.
risk_factors: Open-weight models become economic for Anthropic's largest customers as GPU rents and Chinese token prices fall.
Falling token prices compress margins: compute rose to 58% of sales and revenue per compute dollar fell to $1.72.
The frontier lead can be copied through distillation and is discounted at launch.
Valuation of 9x to 13x 2027 sales and about 39x 2028 EPS requires roughly 69x revenue growth over three years.
Partners Amazon and Alphabet are also competitors and own the storefronts that sell nearly half of Anthropic's revenue.
Regulation risk from windfall profits and data center restrictions.
Breach of AI safeguards or a cyberattack, which Morgan Stanley calls the most underpriced risk.
Post-IPO slump risk, with SpaceX down about 30% from its high.
vol_and_positioning: Hedge funds are 11 points underweight tech.
ANT indicated up to 24% higher on the gray market, with Nasdaq 100 futures up 2%.
Oversubscription is described as the largest in IPO history, with some buyers using ANT as a hedge against AI disruption.
geopolitical: The White House alleged in July that Moonshot distilled Anthropic's Fable model.
A federal crackdown on open-weight models is described as more likely, with David Sacks saying Anthropic's allies wanted it.
Midterm voters passed measures to ban, cap or slow data centers.
cross_bank_references: Goldman's 'Token Prices Are Falling Faster Than Demand' warning (Sep 3) is starting to look less like a forecast and more like a 10-Q.
Bloomberg Intelligence's valuation of about $1.5 trillion is higher than Seaport's $1.35 trillion share-count basis.

tension_points.bull_case: Seaport says self-hosting only pays above $2.4 million a year, and Haiku at $0.20 per million tokens is cheaper than open-weight alternatives in almost all cases, so most customers stay.
tension_points.bear_case: The largest customers, who carry the most revenue, can rationally self-host, DeepSeek V4 Pro falls to about $0.50 per million tokens at scale, and falling GPU rents lower the breakeven.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A cut in hyperscaler GPU rental prices lowers the $2.4 million breakeven and pulls more customers into self-hosting. Anthropic's frontier lead failing to hold also breaks the thesis.

tension_points.bull_case: Bloomberg Intelligence says the pricing reflects recursive self-improvement lowering compute costs, drug discovery expansion, first-party agents and enterprise adoption.
tension_points.bear_case: At 9x to 13x 2027 sales and about 39x 2028 EPS, the valuation sits above megacaps at 3x to 6x and requires about 69x revenue growth by 2028 while token prices fall.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The Q4 print showing whether Anthropic held margins or price, as the article says the next couple of quarterly reports will show which one gave.

theme_stances.key_argument: The valuation pays for the largest customers at frontier margins, and those customers can already use open-weight alternatives.

theme_stances.key_argument: Seaport says self-hosting does not make economic sense for most customers, but the argument depends on the frontier lead holding.
theme_stances.evidence: for the vast majority of customers, self-hosting does not make economic sense
